utterances.text: Can you recall perhaps that on the 28th of March of 2001, Ms. Del Ponte, the chief Prosecutor made a public announcement to the effect that she believed that should serious violations of international humanitarian law were committed, the Tribunal would have jurisdiction over the territory of Macedonia, can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Not specifically, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I can assist again. If the witness could be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D626. It has an ERN starting with 1D00-5590.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is under tab 8 of the binder. Mr. Tucker, I will come back on the first few pages of this document a little bit later. But we can see from the title of that first page that it contains a list of materials given by the Macedonian authorities during the visit of the chief Prosecutor to Skopje on 20 November 2001. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will come back in a moment to the list of document provided to you. But at this stage I would ask the registry to go to page 1D00-5598, please. This document contains a number of summaries of statement and comments made by different international players and in this page there is one attributed to Madam Del Ponte dated the 28th of March of 2001. And I would like to start with the second paragraph of this statement where Madam Del Ponte said that: "It is not clear whether crimes of war were committed and expressed hope that the existing of this court jurisdiction will act as a warning and will prevent those criminal acts." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there is a comment attributed directly to her which reads: "I hope that all questions will be resolved in a peaceful and democratic manner, she said. And pointed out that if the war crimes are committed, the Tribunal in The Hague will begin an investigation to resolve these crimes." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's another comment attributed to Ms. Del Ponte which says: "Madam Del Ponte said that as soon as possible an investigation team will be sent to work with the Macedonian authorities in finding out what is happening in the country. And in the meantime, the Tribunal will maintain close contact with the authorities in Macedonia for exchanging information about its activities." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I don't wish to ask you to comment upon the accuracy or otherwise of the content, but do you recall Madam Del Ponte making that statement at the time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that on the 9th of November of 2001, the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal announced the formal opening of an investigation into the events of Ljuboten and Nepostreno. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Could you repeat the date, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The 9th of November, 2001.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, I don't believe that is correct, sir. I may be wrong but to my knowledge the official investigation wasn't opened until the first few months of the following year.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I'll ask the registry, then, to show what is now Exhibit P391.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this has already been admitted. This is a Prosecution request for deferral --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is under tab 24 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will draw your attention to page 3 of that document, Mr. Tucker, if I may. This is N000-9883-0. And I will draw your attention to paragraph 3 of the Prosecution request. I will read it out to you, it says this: "On 9 November 2001, the Prosecution formally commenced an investigation into allegations concerning the activities of the NLA, National Liberation Army in Macedonia during 2001 including the existence of a number of mass graves involving Macedonian civilian victims killed in Neprosteno." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "On the same date, the Prosecutor also formally commenced an investigation into allegations concerning the activities of Macedonian forces against Macedonian Albanian civilians in Macedonia during 2001 including the alleged crimes committed in Ljuboten. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree, I hope, that the investigation or the formal opening of the investigation, of the Prosecutor's investigation into the events of Ljuboten took place on the 9th of November of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That is correct. I was mistaken. It was her exerting her primacy over the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, simply for the record I will indicate that this date the 9th of November, 2001 was also the date noted and taken into consideration by the Trial Chamber in its decision of 4 October 2002, for the deferral of five cases, including the case Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall, Mr. Tucker, that a few days later on the 21st of November of 2001, the chief Prosecutor Madam Del Ponte actually formally announced the opening of the investigation into the Ljuboten events, or you don't recall?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't recall, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree that all through the year of 2001 and 2002 your office, the Office of the Prosecutor received assistance and support in relation to your Ljuboten and Neprosteno investigation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I still don't agree with that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can you agree then that in late August of 2001, I believe on the 31st of 2001 [sic], the state prosecutor appointed a liaison person to be the contact person for the ICTY do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, my first involvement in Macedonia I think I said earlier was in November of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you recall a person by the name Maja Konevska?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can, but I'm not sure in what context, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I will show you a document in a minute which may assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But perhaps for the record at line -- at page 51, line 25, there is a reference to the 31st of 2001, it should be the 31st of August of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is it correct that one particular way in which the Macedonian authorities provided assistance to your office was by providing you with information documents and material which were relevant to your investigations into the events of Ljuboten and Neprosteno. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I know the Macedonian authorities supplied numerous documents to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And among that information or material that was provided to you by the Macedonian authorities and here, Mr. Tucker, I only talk of 2001 and 2002, you would agree that some of that material pertained to the Ljuboten incidents. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't know specifically the dates. The first documents I was aware of were in 2002, but I don't discount the possibility there being documents supplied earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is a number of particular document that I would wish to ask you at this stage and would you agree or can you agree that no later than 18 -- I'm being prompted by my colleague to slow down, Mr. Tucker, which I shall duly do. Is that correct, Mr. Tucker, that no later than the 18th of September of 2001, your office was in possession of the report of the commission set up by Mr. Boskoski to look into the events of Ljuboten. Can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can't again, sir, my first involvement with the Macedonian situation was in November of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll ask the registry to show Mr. Tucker what is Rule 65 ter 1D654. It has an ERN 1D005870, this document has a Macedonian translation which is 1D00-5864. This is tab number 9, Mr. Tucker. It seems to be under tab 10, Your Honour, perhaps in your binder. There may be a slight difference. Your Honour, I will simply explain for the record one different translation of this document is already in evidence. The reason for using this particular translation - and I will ask the registry kindly to go back to the previous version - may become apparent in a second, but ... Mr. Tucker, do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: My document at tab 9 --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Is the 000 -- sorry, 0011 document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's the document. Mr. Tucker, do you recognise this document as the report prepared by the commission set up by Mr. Boskoski to look into the events of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't believe that I have seen this document before, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, at this stage I will simply ask you, perhaps, to focus on the very top of that document. And in particular, in the fax line that appears at the very top of that document. Can you see the fax line?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says and I will read it: September 18, 2001; 1602; from UN ICTY and then there's a telephone number. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the Macedonian original, a few page later, 1D00-5864 and again at the top of the page you will see there's again the same fax line. A little bit later at 1605. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that these documents came from your own office, UN ICTY. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Without being able to confirm the telephone number, I couldn't actually -- I have not seen the document before, so I can't really confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that the fax line at the top indicates that it came from, in any case, a UN ICTY office?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: If we assume the documents are genuine, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think we need to tender this other translation. It's simply relevant the record will reflect the matter which we want it to underline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I hope you can agree, sir, that in light of the nature of the material that is provided there, this material must have come from the Ministry of Interior. Can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's what it says on the translated document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I should put it more fairly to you. I will ask the registry to bring up what is Rule 65 ter 282. It has an ERN of N001-8564 there is a Macedonian translation, N001-8564, MF. Mr. Tucker, that should be under tab 10 of your binder and I will ask you a bit later about those requests for assistance which you called RFA, as I understand. At this stage, I would like to go to the second page of the document. Simply for you to confirm that this particular request for assistance from your office, the Office of the Prosecutor to the Macedonian authorities was prepared or sent on the 13th of January of 2005, and was signed by senior trial attorney Mr. Andrew Cayley. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we may go back to the first page, please. I'll ask to you focus on the third paragraph of that document. It says this: "Among the analysed material provided to the OTP by the Ministry of the Interior of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia is a report of the commission formed with the decision number 07-581/01, on 13 August 2001." And then there is a paragraph which comes from this report. Would you agree, Mr. Tucker, that this in fact is the same report as was mentioned earlier in this statement reveals or indicates that the document had come from the minister of interior?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I think without -- without being able to read the document completely and then compare it with -- it is a very difficult comment for me to make because I'm not familiar with the former document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will simply ask you to turn back to tab 9 for a minute. And it refers to a particular number on the first page and that number is 07-581-01, would you confirm that this is the same number as the one mentioned on your RFAs. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It is the same number.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. And I suppose, then, that you can agree that the report prepared by the commission set up by Mr. Boskoski was available your office no less or no later than two weeks after it had rendered its report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: By referring to the contents of the RFA we referred to, it would appear so, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose that you can also agree with the proposal that the Ministry of Interior which provided you with that document was not exactly trying to hide from you the efforts that had been made to uncover what had happened in Ljuboten but that they proactively informed you about this. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Again, without familiarising myself with both documents, I think would be very rash of me to make any comment on that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I would simply ask you if you can to comment upon the fact that the Ministry of Interior provided you that information. I'm not asking you, Mr. Tucker, to make any comment about the content of the document. It would be unfair to you. But would you agree that, in this case, the Ministry of Interior in fact proactively sought to provide with you information pertaining to the work that they had carried out in this matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Certainly correct to say that a report was submitted and received by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it was submitted by the Ministry of Interior, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct or is that within your knowledge, sir, that on the same date, the 18th of September of 2001, again, at the latest you were provided with other information by the Ministry of Interior concerning their effort to find out what had happened in Ljuboten. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't, sir. I think it is appropriate for me to say that my involvement with this particular issue extended from November 2001 until the conclusion of the exhumation and autopsies.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: -- with the exception -- I beg your pardon, with the exception then of the submission of certain articles to the Dutch Forensic Institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that. But I will seek your assistance in relation to another document, if I may, Mr. Tucker, and that is under tab 11 of your binder. This is a document which is MFI as 1D146, N000-0021, the Macedonian being N000-0017. Mr. Tucker, again I won't, in view of your previous answers I won't ask you to comment on the content of the documents but I would kindly ask you, again, to look at the very top of the document. Again there is a fax line there. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you will see that it mentions the same date as the previous document, that is the September 18 of 2001. The time is one minute before the other fax, 1601, and it again comes from UN ICTY with a fax number. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose you can agree again in view of the title that you can read on the document and in view of our previous discussion that this document must have come again from the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that during the relevant time or the relevant period I'm again talking of 2001 and 2002 when as far as you can testify to that, you received information pertaining to the Ljuboten incident from other state organs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can you recall in particular that on the 18th of November of 2001, the then state prosecutor or public prosecutor Mr. Stavre Dzikov provided you with information which the Macedonian authorities had collected in relation to the events of Ljuboten. Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't remember the specifics, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness, please, be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D626 this is under tab 8 of the binder, it has an ERN of 1D005-590.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Before you dive into the document, Mr. Tucker, are you aware of preliminary meetings taking place between your office, the Office of the Prosecutor and the competent state organs of Macedonia in relation to the events of Ljuboten taking place sometime in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Not directly no, sir. I am aware that they must have taken place but I'm not aware of the specifics.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware, perhaps, of a particular meeting between Mr. Matti Raatikainen and the state prosecutor Mr. Dzikov late in August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: With the assistance of the registry, if we can go to page 4 of that document, that would be 1D00-5593.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is tab 8 and this will be the fourth page of this document. As you can see from the top of that document, this is a document or a letter coming from the public prosecution office of the Republic of Macedonia. This is dated November 18th, 2001. And it is directed to Madam Carla Del Ponte, the Prosecutor General of the ICTY through the office in Skopje, Mr. Szydlik. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps just to put the letter in its proper context. Mr. Dzikov says the following: "Within the frame of the cooperation between the international organisations and institutions, the public prosecution office of the Republic of Macedonia and the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia in fight against organised crime have had a number of contacts and meetings with the representatives of the international organisations and institutions." And then there are two other paragraphs. I would like to draw also your attention to the last paragraph on that page. It says that: "On June 26th 2001, in the premises of the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia, the public prosecutor met Mr. Andrzej Szydlik, an operational officer of the ICTY in the Republic of Macedonia. I'll stop here for a second, Mr. Tucker. Were you aware of that particular meeting between Mr. Szydlik and Mr. Dzikov on the 26th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'd ask you to turn now to the next page. It would be 5594. And then Mr. Dzikov records another meeting between himself and Mr. Raatikainen. It says: "On August 29, 2001, again in his office, the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia met Mr. Matti Raatikainen an investigative team chief --" Perhaps I will stop there for a minute. You can confirm that Matti Raatikainen is one of your colleagues, is that correct? Or was one of your colleague.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, he was actually my supervisor. He was the investigative team leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. And the letter goes on to say this: "We have both considered all possible ways of mutual cooperation having the aim of efficient collection of evidences for criminal offenses committed against humanity and the international law." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "So that we can indict offenders who have committed or have ordered the committal of severe violences against the 1949 Geneva Conventions on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia in the course of this year." It goes on to say this: "Mr. Raatikainen informed that the Tribunal started to interview several persons regarding the events in Macedonia and the report on the interview has been already submitted. "They have started, he said, to do researching and procedures to officially conduct an investigation in the Republic of Macedonia for the criminal offences under the jurisdiction of the Tribunal." Were you aware of that particular meeting, Mr. Tucker?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I was not, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And were you privy to the content of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then in the next paragraph it say this: "The deputy public prosecutor Madam Maja Konevska has been assigned for your correct and comprehensive informing. She is in charge for the direct contacts and complete cooperation with the representatives of the ICTY's office in Skopje to prosecute offenders who have committed offences prescribed in the international law and coming under the jurisdiction of the Tribunal.'? And I think you have indicated already that you were not aware at the time that Mr. Konevska [sic] had been assigned that role as a liaison officer or was a contact person with the ICTY. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph, Mr. Dzikov also indicates that he is attaching information pertaining to the events of Ljuboten in the period from August 10, 11, 12 to August the 14th. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We will go into this material in a moment, Mr. Tucker, but first I would like to ask you about this meeting. Would you agree that the meeting between Mr. Raatikainen, your former superior, and Mr. Dzikov was intended to provide for means and ways of cooperations between the state prosecutor and the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And from that letter I can also see that at the time Mr. Raatikainen had informed the state prosecutor that the Office of the Prosecutor, your office, had started interviewing witnesses in relation to incident occurring in the country. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also informed the local authorities through Mr. Dzikov that the Prosecution had in fact started to do researching and procedure to officially conduct an investigation in the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps we will seek to tender this document at this stage. We will come back to it on a number of occasion but that may be simpler, perhaps, to tender it at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D198, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, were you aware of the fact that this particular meeting of the 29th of August of 2001 between Mr. Dzikov and Mr. Raatikainen had been publicised in Macedonia. Were you aware of that fact?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D623. It has an ERN of 1D00-5579, 5578 in Macedonian. And, Mr. Tucker, it should be under tab 7A, like Alan, in your binder. And you see this is, again, a document coming from the office of the public prosecutor of Macedonia. It is dated the 31st of August of 2001. It is directed to the public media with a title of announcement. And if you focus on the first paragraph it says that on 29 August of 2001, the Macedonian public prosecutor, Mr. Stavre Dzikov had a work meeting with Mr. Matti Raatikainen, leader of the ICTY investigation team. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to go to the second paragraph of that document. It says that Mr. Raatikainen informed that: "Since March this year, ICTY had started to monitor the events in the Republic of Macedonia and that a month ago a few persons were interviewed in and a report was sent to the ICTY. Thus, an investigation had commenced and the procedure was open for the beginning of an official process of investigation in the Republic of Macedonia into committed crimes which are in the jurisdiction of the international Tribunal." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D199, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you have already indicated to me that you couldn't remember the exact date, I believe, of Madam Del Ponte's visit to the Republic of Macedonia. Can you agree, however, that Madam Del Ponte visited the area towards the end of November of 2001, together with a group of members of the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm sure the events would be well publicised, but I can't comment on the actual timing of the event, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you can confirm and perhaps I will show you again the document which is under tab 8 of your binder which is now Exhibit 1D198. You can agree, Mr. Tucker, that during that visit and the document records it on the 20th of November of 2001, the Prosecutor was provided with a set of documents by the Macedonian authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Which document is this, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This would be tab number 8 in your binder, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the second page of this document, please. Can you agree that under number 7 of this document there's a reference to information regarding the events in the vicinity of the Skopje village of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And we will come back later to this document but simply for your assistance, if we can turn to page 1D00-5615 of this document. You would agree, sir, that this appears to be a document from the public prosecution office of the Republic of Macedonia, dated the 18th of November of 2001 and it concerns the events that happened in the area of the village Ljuboten, Skopje, in the period August 10, 11, 12, and 14th, 2001. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We can put that document aside for a moment. We will come back to it in a moment. Is that correct that in 2002 and in the years that followed, the Office of the Prosecutor solicited material and information from the Macedonian authorities which pertained among other things to the Ljuboten events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I am aware that that is so, although I wasn't directly involved with that investigation at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And from a formal point of view, would you agree that many of those questions are made in the form of request for assistance, RFA, of the same sort that we have seen a bit earlier?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And although that may be an obvious question for you, Mr. Tucker, would you agree that those RFAs are being sent by the Prosecution to the authorities which the Prosecution understand to be able to provide them with the material mentioned in these RFAs. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. There is a set protocol for the submission of RFAs to member countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you able to confirm the proposition that in the period between the 12th of August of 2001 and the month of May of 2002, the Office of the Prosecution only sent one particular RFA to the Macedonian authority. Is that correct, or is that something you have within your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: It's not something I can comment on, sir. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I will assist by pointing to a particular document which is under tab 12 of your binder, Mr. Tucker. It is Rule 65 ter 1D669, 1D00-5925.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document that was provided to us by the Office of the Prosecutor upon our request earlier this year. This is a document that records the RFAs sent to the government of the Republic of Macedonia covering the period August 2001 to January 2007, as can be seen from the top of the page. I believe that this would be the third page in the version that is on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the table, Mr. Tucker, are you able to confirm that the first entry in that particular document is dated the 30th of January of 2002, and follows an RFA number INV/T/9141/AC/TL/MR-T 07-TL 12. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And will you agree at least from on the basis of that document and the information provided to us by the Office of the Prosecution that this was the first document or the first request for information sent by the Office of the Prosecution to the Macedonian authorities since August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask you, sir, now to turn to tab 30 -- 13, I apologise, 1-3 --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- of this binder. As you can see this is a letter which has a format slightly different from the previous document that was shown to you in the more formalised form of an RFA, but I hope that you can confirm that this is a letter sent to the multi-lateral organisation section of the ministry of foreign affairs of the Republic of Macedonia; that is dated the 30th of January of 2002; and that it is signed, again, by Mr. Andrew Cayley, STA for the Office of the Prosecutor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look, perhaps, on the first page on the top left-hand corner of that document you will agree, I hope, that the number of that document is the same as the one that I showed you in the previous document in the table that was provided to us by the Prosecution. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I may ask you to turn to the next document in your binder that would be Rule 65 ter 1D655. It has an ERN 1D00-5876. And I will ask you that, is that correct or is that within your knowledge that because you had not received a formal or complete response from the authorities from the ministry of foreign affairs, at that time you sent a second request or a reminder, I should say, in relation to the document that we've seen a bit earlier and that this reminder is the document that you have now in front of you. Can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: This is tab 13A, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the date of the document that is the 5th of August of 2002, it is again coming from Mr. Cayley, STA of the Office of the Prosecution, and it is sent again to the ministry of foreign affairs of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the first paragraph of the document, Mr. Cayley's referring again to the same number, the reference number of the previous RFA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in the second paragraph he says: "We note that no response has been received to date; therefore, we kindly ask you to provide us with a reply by 30th of September 2003, and to quote our reference." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, did you ever found out or did you every take an interest in finding out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, my apologise for interrupting. Just perhaps a comment or a suggestion. Perhaps just so that the transcript in months ahead will be clear, perhaps my colleague could formulate his questions to the witness when he is asking -- when he uses the word "you" in a question a few minutes ago, I think my colleague is referring to the Office of the Prosecutor. And I'm just wondering whether the record may be clearer in the future if my colleague could use the term of the OTP or the Office of the Prosecutor in that context. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon is probably quite right, Your Honour. I believe the "you's" in most cases had to do with the Office of the Prosecutor. I will specify when the question refers particularly to yourself, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can look at the documents on the -- well, let me ask the question again. Did you ever find out or did information ever come in your possession as to the reason why the ministry of foreign affairs of the Republic of Macedonia had been unable to provide you with the information that had been sought by Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Unfortunately, sir, I can't answer that. My involvement I mentioned earlier was only from November 2001 until April/May of 2003 -- 2002. And purely on the basis of monitoring the exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case I will show you the next document at this stage, which is under tab 13B of your binder. It is Rule 65 ter 1D656. And it has an ERN of 1D00-5877. Are you aware of the fact, sir, that when the ministry of foreign affairs appeared to be unable to provide the material sought by the Office of the Prosecutor, you directed a request to Mr. Dzikov, the state prosecutor. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it, sir, but that wouldn't be unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you to look at the document now in front of you. You will see it is -- or I will ask you to confirm that, again, this is entitled a second reminder RFA 12. That is dated the 14th of October of 2002. That it is signed by Patrick Lopez-Terres, chief of investigations and that it is directed Mr. Stavre Dzikov, prosecutor general of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you look at the first paragraph of this document, it again refers to the same RFA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the letter of Mr. Lopez-Terres says that: "We note that no response has been received to date; therefore, we ask you to provide a rely no later than 30 October 2002, and to quote our reference." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would kindly request Defence counsel to speak a little bit slower. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Tucker. The record hasn't picked up your answer.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful. Are aware of the fact that when asked about this, the state prosecutor Mr. Dzikov informed the Office of the Prosecution that they had looked carefully for the material requested, that they had provided you with the material that they had already received or been able to locate and that they continued looking for this material. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is -- that not be the document. Mr. Tucker, I will come back to that in the -- after the break. Is it correct that after you have sent a request for information to the Macedonian authorities or for that matter to any state authorities, it is not your responsibility, and by that I mean the Office of the Prosecutor, to figure out or to investigate where, in effect, the information will be coming from within the state institutions?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I think as a general rule is that correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in other words although some material may say come back from the ministry of foreign affairs, the material in question might have been obtained or might have been generated by another organ or institution of the state. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am mindful of the time and I wonder whether that is the proper time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we can accommodate your hope, Mr. Mettraux. It's a little early, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That would allow me to locate the document in question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will be able, then, to have a break now, resuming at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The reason for the mysterious disappearance of the previous document has been established, Your Honour. We had sought not to scare the Chamber by distributing only one binder today to Your Honours. The document is in a second binder which we will provide to you tomorrow. However, we have identified the number of the document and it is an exhibit already. It is Exhibit 1D75.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Tucker, we'll walk backward a little bit into the questions. I apologise, I'll ask you for this particular document to look at it on the screen. As can you see from the top left-hand corner this is again a document that comes from the public prosecution of the Republic of Macedonia. It is dated the 14th of August of 2002. It is addressed to Madam Carla Del Ponte, ICTY OTP and the subject is response to the request for information submitted by the Prosecutor of the ICTY. You will recall a moment ago before the break asked you if you could recall a response by the state prosecutor, Mr. Dzikov to your request and I mean the requests of the Office of the Prosecutor for particular information. And I was asking more specifically whether you could recall a response by Mr. Dzikov to the effect that they had looked for the material in question carefully, that they had identified and provided some of it and that they continued to look for it. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask the registry to go to the fourth page of that particular document. This would be N000-9915. It is page 4. This would be a few pages down the line, please. Thank you. That is the right page. Mr. Tucker, I will ask to you look at the last paragraph on this page and perhaps it could be expanded a bit for you to be able to read it. This is the paragraph starting with the words: "In relation to the repeated request." And perhaps before I start reading this paragraph for the transcript, Mr. Tucker, can you recall now that one of the documents that I had shown to you a reminder, RFA reminder was dated the 5th of August of 2002. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And for the transcript I will read the response of Mr. Dzikov. He says this: "In relation to the repeated request, dated 5 August 2002, with reference number NSK-630-02 of the prosecutor of the International Tribunal, in accordance with Rule 8 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Tribunal, to forward to the international Court all relevant information in relation to the investigations and criminal proceedings related to the above-mentioned cases and all relevant investigation and other official files of the authorities of the Republic of Macedonia, including all relevant court records, the public prosecutor of the Republic of Macedonia informs you that up to date most correctly and most conscientiously has forwarded all relevant information in his possession to the Prosecutor of the International Tribunal. Including concrete material written evidence and, at the same time, the interest is existing to continue forwarding all relevant information." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then he says: "With regard to the relevant court records, you should address the court which was most conscientiously cooperating until now having in mind the position of the court in the Republic of Macedonia." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd seek to not tender this document, since it is already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, you have indicated earlier in response to my question that it wasn't your responsibility, the responsibility of your office to look into the internal functioning of a particular state or government and that this was essentially for the authorities to figure out. Do you recall telling me that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in relation in particular to the Ljuboten or Neprosteno matter for that matter, if material was received by the Prosecution from, say, the ministry of foreign affairs, you would have no indication or no reason to believe that the material could not have come in fact from another institution; that is, that the ministry of foreign affairs obtained it from another organ of the state. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, that I believe to be true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And in this particular case, it could well be the case that some of the information provided to you by the Macedonian authorities had come from the Ministry of the Interior of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That is possible, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is also possible that some of the material which was eventually sent to the Office of the Prosecutor by the Macedonian authorities had been provided by Mr. Boskoski as minister of the interior directly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't know -- I don't know if that is true. I guess it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: My objection is -- is the following. Virtually anything is possible, Your Honours, and I think perhaps the question, perhaps to make it helpful to the Trial Chamber should be rephrased perhaps -- should, was it likely, was it probable because quite frankly anything in this world is possible, although there are many, many, many things that are very unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Even that the evidence in this case will finish next week, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That would also be unlikely, Your Honour. Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I think I rely on the Court's rules of likelihood rather than Mr. Saxon. But I will put the question, perhaps, more squarely to yourself, Mr. Tucker, and in doing that, I will ask the registry to show to Mr. Tucker which is already Exhibit P402. It has an ERN N000-9704-ET-01. We believe the Macedonian version would start at page 98 and 99.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this would be under tab 14, 1-4, of your binder.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: This is a translation of an expert or excerpt or a chapter of the book written by Mr. Boskoski. It has been provided to us by the Prosecution. If you look at the first page of that particular excerpt, Mr. Tucker, you will see that Mr. Boskoski in his book mentioned that in the year of 2001 and 2002, he had intensive meetings and then follows a list of particular individuals, internationals, and your name appears in this list. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I suppose that you can recall having met with our client on quite a number of occasions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I certainly can for the 2001. I can't recall anything in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately how many times you met with Mr. Boskoski at the time?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I would imagine maybe half a dozen times at various meetings, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And some of those meetings, you will agree, had to do with the issue of the Ljuboten investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I actually can't remember any discussions about Ljuboten. My recollections are in connection with Neprosteno.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will come back to that in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But if I may ask the registry to turn to the second page of that particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I will ask to you do the same, Mr. Tucker, the next page of this particular document. And if I may draw your attention on the first full paragraph of this book and I will read it for the transcript. It says this: "On one occasion I was thanked for the good collaboration and abundant material which we had delivered to The Hague Tribunal. My interlocutor emphasised that he knew Macedonia was going through very difficult times and that The Hague Tribunal had not opened any proceedings at all. But in terms of human rights violations, he added, one of the ambiguous cases in Ljuboten would need to be investigated. I replied that the Macedonian authorities stood at the Tribunal disposal and would provide all the facts available to help clarify this case which certain individuals were exploiting with the aim of having me directly indicted." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree that at least from this passage of Mr. Boskoski's book, it would suggest that material had been provided by his ministry to The Hague Tribunal with his knowledge and possibly, since we are in the realm of possibilities, with his approval. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: According to this paragraph, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Tucker, that immediately after the events in Ljuboten your office had obtained information from various sources as to what had happened in the village?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I beg your pardon, this is after the exhumation, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, before, I'm sorry. I will put the question again to you. Is that correct that within days of the incident in Ljuboten which happened between the 10th, 12th of August of 2001, your office obtained information pertaining to that particular incident. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 129. It has an ERN N000-9235 in the English, and it is N000-9235, MF, in the Macedonian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is under tab 15, 1-5, of your binder. If I can ask you, perhaps, by starting at the very bottom of that document, you will see it is a so-called morning press summaries. And if you look at the footer of that document you will see that it is-- it says it has been prepared by ICTY Skopje TOB. Can you assist us, what does TOB means?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm trying to find that on the document, sir. The -- under the title residents flee from Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. Tucker, yes. If you look at the footer down it says: "Prepared by ICTY Skopje TOB." Do you know what "TOB" stands for?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, I don't, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In any case, the date of that particular document is Wednesday, the 15th of August of 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's the date, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I ask to you perhaps look or scan through briefly this particular section of the document which you identified under the title residents flee from Ljuboten 'Sunday's' victims buried, you will agree that this document contains information - true or false - about what is said to have happened in the village of Ljuboten during that weekend. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And from the footer of that document, again, I suppose you will agree that this information would have been in your possession at the latest on 15th of August, 2001. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can't authenticate the documents, so I'm not sure how I can possibly say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree that this is -- the footer of that document suggests that this indeed was the case?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: It does, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you it turn to tab 16 of your binder, and if I may ask the registry to bring up what is Exhibit 238. P238. Are you aware, sir, that within a few days, again I'm talking of the 10th to the 12th and following days of August of 2001, your office came in possession of information pertaining to the events of Ljuboten through the OSCE, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, I became aware of that in 2002, early 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you also capable of confirming that this particular information which you have in front of you, which is a spot report pertaining to this incident, was provided to your office no later than the 20th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't know when it was delivered, but I am aware of the contents of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps I will ask you to look at the very top of that document once against, Mr. Tucker. It has, again, a fax line which indicates that the document came from UN ICTY. It has again the same telephone number as the previous document and the date, 20 August 2001 at 1429. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, perhaps, I should have asked you that. Are you familiar with this particular document?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I think the -- I'd be safer to say the contents of the document rather than the document itself, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware that the content of this document suggests that five men in civilian clothes were found dead in the village of Ljuboten during that weekend. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct, Mr. Tucker, that no later than the 21st of September of 2001, your office, the ICTY OTP, had received a report from Human Rights Watch pertaining to the event of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In that case, I will just ask you to turn to the next tab in your binder that. Is tab 17, 1-7.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is it Exhibit P352, it's already been admitted through Mr. Bouckaert.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is the cover letter of the report written and prepared by Human Rights Watch concerning the events of Ljuboten. And as can you see from the cover page, the report itself was sent to Mr. Morton Bergsmore [phoen] Of the legal officer in the OTP. The letter is date 6 of September of 2001, and if I can ask you to look at the bottom right of the document there is stamp saying ICTY investigations, 21st September, 2001. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And that would suggest, wouldn't it, that this particular document was received no later than 21st September, 2001 by the OTP. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct. I can confirm the stamp, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that also correct or are you familiar perhaps with the contents, perhaps, of the Human Rights Watch report in relation to the events of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And are you aware of the fact that allegations are being made in the report that a massacre took place in Ljuboten and that individuals who committed crimes in that village had been under the authority of Mr. Boskoski at that time, are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We have discussed a number of contact which you had with the Macedonian authorities concerning, generally, the Ljuboten and Neprosteno investigations. Is that also correct that you sought assistance or cooperation from the Macedonian authorities in relation to the exhumation process at Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir. We sought the cooperation of the Macedonian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the Macedonian authorities agreed to provide you this assistance. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: They agreed to undertake the -- the exhumation process.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you, the Office of the Prosecutor, or representative of that office also made it clear to the authorities at the time that their assistance to allow you to enter into the village was critical for your own investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's not to my knowledge, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is under tab 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, this is Exhibit 1D35. This is, again, an investigator's note and I will simply ask you to turn to the third page to confirm again that it has been prepared by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is tab 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, can you confirm that this particular investigator's notes has, again, been prepared by you?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, I can, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we can go back to the first page, we will see again that the purpose is similar to the purpose of the other such meeting which we have already gone through. It is a meeting arranged by Mr. Szydlik, operation officer of the ICTY for the visit of Mr. Dennis Milner, deputy chief of investigations. It again took place on the 27th of November of 2001 at 9.45 in the office of the OSCE in Skopje. And in attendance were Sandra Mitchell, senior member of the OSCE, Mr. Palmer and Canavan again from the OSCE, Mr. Milner, Mr. Szydlik and yourself. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we may turn to the second page of that document, please. And I will ask you, Mr. Tucker, to focus on the last paragraph of that document which starts with the words: "DM stated that MR."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honour, DM would be Mr. Dennis Milner, deputy chief of investigations and Mr. MR is Mr. Tucker's former superior, Mr. Raatikainen who the documents indicate was not present but mention during the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, the passage in question says the following: "Denis Milner stated that Matti Raatikainen had basic details in The Hague for both investigations: Neprosteno and Ljuboten. He felt that it was important for the ICTY and OSCE to continue the liaison over these issues. It was vital to ICTY investigators obtain access to these areas to conduct their investigations. Personal introductions by OSCE would be very useful." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the point that was being made by Mr. Milner in this particular instance, wasn't it, was that the Office of the Prosecutor sought to have access to the village to conduct its own investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: To that village and other areas, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, also, that the --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, perhaps before I move on could we mark this document -- it is an exhibit, I am sorry. I apologise, Mr. Tucker.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that the Macedonian authorities at the time and, I'm again talking of the year 2001 and 2002, made allowance for you to participate as fully as you wished into the collection of information and investigation conducted by the competent Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Sorry, sir, could you repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: In the year 2001 and 2002, is it correct that the competent Macedonian authorities made allowance for the Office of the Prosecutor to be able to participate in whatever aspect of the investigation they wished to be involved in. Is that correct? Or is that something that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it in that context, no, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown once again what is Exhibit P391. This again, Your Honours, is the Prosecution request for deferral of cases dated 5th of September, 2002. And it is under tab 24, Mr. Tucker, of your binder. And I will ask the registry to move to page N000-9883-51. Mr. Tucker, this is one of the documents which the Office of the Prosecutor attached to its application for the deferral of a number of cases to the jurisdiction of the ICTY and this particular document is to be found in annex H, yes, annex H of the document. This is a summary provided by the domestic authorities about each and every case which you had sought deferral for. This would be page N000-9883-51, Mr. Tucker. That would be, I believe, page 61 on the top right-hand corner, if it is easier for your identification.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The particular page, Mr. Tucker, should say case V in Roman, case Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Forgive me, sir. I'm going by the reference number at the top right-hand of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes. And it goes in reverse order, Mr. Tucker, so if you go forward, this would be number 61.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I've got it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask you to focus on this case IV, case Ljuboten, you will see there's a summary of some of the steps taken by the Macedonian authority in relation to the case of Ljuboten. And it starts by saying that: "On September 10th, principle public prosecutor office Skopje addressed to the investigative judge from the principle Court Skopje with request for initiation of an investigation proposing the security measures concerning the events happened in locality called Ljubotenski Bacila." And then there is a description of this particular event and I would like to bring you're attention to a sentence that starts with the phrase: "On August 14, 2001 at 1255 hours, the Ministry of Interior informed deputy public prosecutor and the investigative judge that there are five dead bodies in the village Ljuboten." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "The ministry immediately informed an expert team composed of the magistrate judge of the principle Court Skopje II, Skopje, principle public prosecutor and experts from the Ministry of Interior to examine the site." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It goes on to say: "Besides the continuous monitoring activities of the security situation in the village by the Ministry of the Interior, the expert team did not succeed to examine the site. There were constant shootings and movement of uniformed armed terrorist groups, so the expert teams did not ever reach the site nor have carry out their legal authorisations out of security reasons to examine the site where five people, terrorists, members of the so-called NLA were killed." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes to say: "After this, the Ministry of Interior has informed them that the local villagers already buried the bodies but not on the local village graveyard." And then there's a passage that I don't need to read for the transcript. But the last paragraph on this page starts with the word: "After this, in procedure was included a team of Prosecutor from the International Criminal Court that was done to allow to the Prosecutor of ICTY, Ms. Carla Del Ponte to carry out her own parallel investigation and help according to Article 18 from the statute and Rule 8 from the Rules of Procedure and Evidence." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And at the time, sir, were you aware that this had been done by the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: At the time, are we talking the 5th of September, 2002?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No. I had no involvement in the investigation at that time, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Sorry for the interruption. I see at page 87 of the transcript line 18, the last word of that line should be "parallel", not the word that is there currently. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon is quite right. We don't know the place of Bilovac, but it could in fact -- it should in fact be, "her own parallel investigation." I'm grateful to Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, Mr. Tucker, that the Macedonian authorities had insisted to obtain your assistance with the exhumation process in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I was directed to go there to act as monitor by the Prosecutor, our Prosecutor, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Macedonian authorities had given indication or made submissions to your colleagues that the involvement of the ICTY was perceived as being necessary to enable them to carry out this exhumation?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I wasn't at the time that I -- that I went to the exhumations but that was made perfectly clear to me by the parties when I arrived in Macedonia for both exhumations.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And is that correct that you subjected your agreement or your approval to participate to a number of conditions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours. Again, can it be clarified who "you" is?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Tucker, I'm not suggesting you, personally, decided on the conditions that should be set to the involvement of your office but would it be correct to suggest that the Office of the Prosecutor as an organ of this Tribunal set a number of conditions and put a number of requirements to its approval to participate in the exhumation in Ljuboten. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I'm aware of an agreement that took -- that was arrived at whereby the participation of the ICTY would be -- would be undertaken, yes. I'm not sure if I would class them as conditions. The situation as it was in Macedonia dictated very careful planning and agreement between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps assist you in a minute with those particular conditions or requirements set by the Office of the Prosecution. But you would agree, I suppose, that had those conditions been unacceptable to the Macedonian authorities, the Office of the Prosecutor would have declined to participate in this operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't believe that to be the case at all, sir. I think if there had been any objections by Macedonian authorities to any of the conditions of the agreement, then we would have negotiated until such a time as we found agreement to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct, then, that all of the conditions and requirements set by the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to its involvement were all accepted by the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes. They agreed in full, to my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And perhaps I will ask you to look at a document under tab 18, 1-8, of your binder. This is already an Exhibit, Your Honour. This is 1D42. Mr. Tucker, do you recall that the first time those conditions were put forth by your office was during a meeting on the 30th of January, 2002 with representative of the Macedonian states and other internationals? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't remember the first time or the date sir, but it was -- it's certainly early in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, if I can ask to you look at first, perhaps, the top of this document and for your assistance, Mr. Tucker, this is a document provided to us by your office, the Office of the Prosecutor and it is a NATO declassified or unclassified document. And on the top left-hand corner it says that it concern Ljuboten case, ICTY investigation. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it is dated the 30th of January of 2002 and it refers to a meeting for the Ljuboten case. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can draw your attention to the first paragraph of this document it says that: "On January 30th of 2002, EUMM attended a meeting at the public prosecution department regarding events in Ljuboten on 10/12 August 2001. Among those present were deputy public prosecutor Dragan Cakic, Professor Aleksej Duma of the department of forensic medicine, the president of the appellant court, Ms. Filimena Manevska, your colleague Mr. Andrzej Sydzlik of the ICTY, Ambassador Klaus Voellers of NATO, EUMM and OSCE represented the international community." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says that the prosecutor Mr. Stavre Dzikov chaired the meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That is, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If I can ask to you look at the last paragraph on that document on the bottom of the page, Mr. Tucker, the one starting with the word: The ICTY.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The document say this: "The ICTY presented a number of conditions regarding a possible exhumation in Ljuboten. There should be no uniformed police present at the exhumation site, and no special forces. Security should be provided by NATO in the presence of OSCE and EUMM. Maximum two bodies should be removed from the site at one time, to be taken to Skopje for examination, and then returned to the site before any more bodies were taken to Skopje. The 'Macedonian' presence at the scene should be limited to what would be essential to the investigation. The ICTY should be provided with copies of all relevant documentation, and if relatives of those buried (comment, the identity of the deceased are apparently known) want to be present at the exhumation site, this should be permitted." And if I can ask you to turn the page, Mr. Tucker. "The ICTY requested a written commitment from the authorities to act in compliance with these demands at the request of Mr. Dzikov, Mr. Szydlik promised to present the demands in writing to the authorities. A working meeting between the ICTY and the local authorities, with fewer participants, is envisaged in the near future." As you pointed out, Mr. Tucker, a -- sometime later in fact on the 20th of February of 2002, the agreement that had been reached between Mr. Dzikov and the state prosecutor between yourself, the Office of the Prosecutor, and Mr. Dzikov, the state prosecutor, the Office of the Prosecutor put its conditions or demands in writing to the local authorities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I have a couple of comments, if I may. The extract that you're referring to was a document that was not prepared by the ICTY; it was prepared by EUMM and the phraseology within it is theirs, not ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you would agree that this would reflect the understanding of those present at the meeting that you were setting conditions and demands. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Up to a point. But not exactly, I'm not being awkward, but there was a lot of discussion between ourselves and the Macedonian authorities on how to facilitate this operation to take place. The Macedonian authorities could not go into the area, in fact I think if I remember rightly they refused to go into the area to try to facilitate this operation and we, and particularly me, had to act as a go-between with the villagers and the relatives of the deceased and the family of Ljuboten. So that is a bit of a background to this particular conditions, as you put them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We will go into the issue of the entry into the village in some time, Mr. Tucker. But I should ask you this, were you present at this particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you are not able to say whether the terms, conditions or demands, as they are put down there would fairly represent what was being said during that meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I can ask you turn to tab 19 of your binder, which is already an exhibit as 1D191. Mr. Tucker, this is, I believe, the document which you refer to a moment ago which is a letter of agreement sent by Mr. Patrick Lopez-Terres chief of investigations of the Office of the Prosecutor and it is being sent on the 20th of February of 2002, to Mr. Stavre Dzikov, prosecutor general, Skopje. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: To a point. It was actually signed by Dennis Milner on behalf of Mr. Lopez-Terres.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see that, that's correct. And that would be Dennis Milner, your colleague, who was present during other meetings which we have discussed before. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct. He was deputy chief of investigations at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful.
