If we could go back to the first page of that document, Mr. Tucker, the title of that document is letter of agreement between Office of the Prosecutor, ICTY, and the public prosecutor FYR of Macedonia herein after referred to as the Republic of Macedonia and the letter is addressed to Mr. Dzikov. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it goes on to say this: "Further to previous meetings with representatives of the OTP, and verbal agreements made in relation to events at Ljuboten during 2001, I hereby document and present to you the conditions agreed for the progress of the relevant exhumation and subsequent judicial investigative process." Mr. Tucker, I understand you indicated that you were not present at the meeting of 30th of January of 2002, and I don't mean that as a criticism but you would agree that Mr. Lopez-Terres or, in any case, Mr. Milner conceived of those as being conditions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if we could go down the list of those conditions there's on under number 1 it says that: "The authorities of the Republic of Macedonia agreed to undertake an exhumation of ten marked and identified graves situated in a graveyard at Ljuboten. And acknowledge that the full judicial investigation in relation to the cause of death of the human remains interred at this location has commenced." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the second condition set by your office to its involvement was that during the exhumation and investigation process, no uniformed personnel other than NATO/task force Fox TFF troops will be present at the graveyard site. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The third condition is that personal security during the exhumation process will be undertaken in agreement with and by task force Fox TFF troops to be arranged through the representative of OSCE and EUMM. Is that correct? That's the third condition set.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And under condition number 4, Mr. Lopez-Terres was requesting that no Macedonian special forces, MUP, or military will be involved in the exhumation process. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply for the transcript at page 95 line 4, it should say that special forces, f-o-r-c-e-s. And it should say, "MUP, M-U-P, or military, will be involved in the exhumation process." You have indicated, Mr. Tucker, that you met on a number of occasion with Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript continues to challenge me but referring to MUP which stands for the police with the word "municipal". The transcript should reflect MUP, Your Honour, not municipal. Mr. Tucker, you have indicated that you had met with Mr. Boskoski on a number of occasions and there's one particular meeting which I would like to discuss with you. Can you recall meeting informally with our client in a restaurant in Skopje, a restaurant called Restaurant Uranija and the meeting was attended by your colleague Mr. Szydlik, Mr. Boskoski and Mr. Goran Mitevski. Can you recall that particular meeting?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: The only time I can remember meeting Mr. Boskoski in a restaurant is when he came and was having dinner with Professor Duma and others. I'm not sure if that's the same occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, can you recall a particular meeting which followed the time we just discussed, the end of the month of February, when you and Mr. Boskoski met and Mr. Boskoski and Mr. Mitevski asked you why the police could not be involved in the exhumation process at Ljuboten. Do you recall Mr. Boskoski or Mr. Mitevski asking you this question?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can't, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall indicating to Mr. Boskoski or Mr. Mitevski that you personally, Mr. Tucker, would have no problem with this but that your superior had decided otherwise. Do you recall telling them that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps to clarify this, Mr. Tucker, I understand that the decision was not taken by you, but would you know who decided that the police should not be involved in the exhumation process at Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: When you say the police we had -- we actually had the crime technicians there.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's correct. I referred to the security forces.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I don't know whose decision that was but I would guess it would have been probably Madam Del Ponte's.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But perhaps you will recall another meeting on the 29th of November of 2001 when you met with Prosecutor Dragoljub Cakic do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I have had many meetings. If I met him, I would think there would be an investigator's note there for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: There is indeed. And we'll come to this note in a moment. But can you remember at this stage that there was indeed at the end of November 2001 a meeting, a preparatory meeting for the exhumation process in Ljuboten which was attended by members of the Office of the Prosecutor including yourself and prosecutor Cakic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can't specifically. I thought, from my recollections, that those meetings took place in early 2002, but it may well have taken place at the end of that period that you speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: We will see the investigator's notes in time.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But can you recall that during one of those meetings, you perhaps or in any case, one representative of the Office of the Prosecutor back in November of 2001, had already aired the suggestion coming from you that the security forces of the Republic of Macedonia should not take part in the exhumation operation in Ljuboten. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can vaguely and it is something that's not, I don't think, unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask the registry perhaps to bring up what is Exhibit P55.40, 4-0. Mr. Tucker, this would be under tab 20 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'll ask to you focus on the second of two Official Notes which are mentioned in this particular document. The second one refers to a meeting of 29 of November of 2001. With a previous improvement, it says, from the Prosecution and in the presence of my colleague, Maja, at the premise of the basic public prosecution office number 67, I had met with the representative of The Hague's Tribunal at? The superior prosecution? Previous day on their request. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: I can, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And continues by saying: "During the conversation, I had found that they would like to hear my opinion on their proposal on presence of international security forces at the spot during the exhumation instead of uniformed persons from the Ministry of Interior and also presence of their experts." Can you recall that, Mr. Tucker?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: No, sir, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And it says: "Afterwards, I have told them that I have no authorisation in making decisions on this issue neither are my colleagues, the public prosecutor and the superior prosecutor, I had announced? Criminal procedure? The investigative judge and they to pass this information to their superior and to the court." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HOWARD TUCKER.
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We must adjourn now for the day to resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 20th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.43 p.m.,
